title: Rotary position embeddings
summary: Rotate each pair of query and key coordinates by a position-dependent angle.
why: Makes attention depend on relative offsets without adding a learned position vector to every input.
interview: Prove the rotation identity and reason about context extension.
derivation: Rotations are orthogonal, so R_m transpose is R_-m. Rotations on the same plane compose by adding angles. Apply the identity independently to all dh/2 coordinate pairs.

Changing the RoPE base changes frequency spacing. NTK-aware scaling adjusts the base, while YaRN blends frequency-dependent interpolation and attention scaling. Extension quality needs long-context evaluation.

steps.note: dh must be even; pair ordering must match the model.
Compute trig tables in adequate precision.
Cached key positions must match decode position IDs.

traps: Resetting position IDs during decode corrupts cached attention.
Interleaved and split-half pairing conventions are not interchangeable.
Long context support does not establish reliable retrieval across that entire context.
tradeoff: Extending context grows cache and attention cost; frequency scaling alone does not solve those costs.
code:
import torch

def rotate(x, angle):
    a, b = x.unbind(-1)
    c, s = torch.cos(angle), torch.sin(angle)
    return torch.stack((a*c-b*s, a*s+b*c), dim=-1)

q, k = torch.tensor([1., 2.]), torch.tensor([3., 4.])
m, n = torch.tensor(0.3), torch.tensor(0.8)
assert torch.allclose(rotate(q,m) @ rotate(k,n), q @ rotate(k,n-m))

explanations.title: A rotation per coordinate pair
paragraphs: For each query or key head, group adjacent coordinates into dh/2 two-dimensional planes. At position m, plane j rotates by m times its frequency theta_j. This transforms Q and K while keeping their shape [B,H,S,dh]. Values usually remain unrotated.

For q=(1,0), a 90-degree rotation produces (0,1). The vector norm is unchanged because the rotation matrix is orthogonal. Different coordinate pairs use different frequencies, so the full head encodes position at multiple scales.

RoPE belongs between Q/K projection and attention score computation. Position IDs must remain consistent during prefill, left padding, cache reuse, and decode. Restarting positions at zero for each generated token breaks the intended geometry.

explanations.title: Why the dot product depends on relative position
paragraphs: Transpose reverses an orthogonal rotation. On a fixed coordinate plane, composing two rotations adds their angles. Therefore the query at m and key at n interact through a rotation by (n-m) times that plane frequency. Sum over coordinate planes to obtain the complete head dot product.

This identity concerns the positional transformation of fixed q and k. Actual contextual q and k also depend on token content and preceding layers. RoPE does not make an entire language model invariant to arbitrary reordering or guarantee perfect extrapolation.

explanations.title: Position interpolation, NTK-aware scaling, and YaRN
paragraphs: If training covered positions up to L, directly using much larger positions exposes attention to phase patterns it did not learn. Position interpolation compresses new positions by a factor s, preserving a familiar range while reducing the separation of nearby positions.

NTK-aware base scaling changes the frequency schedule rather than uniformly shrinking every angle. YaRN uses frequency-dependent interpolation and extrapolation with an attention scaling adjustment. Different dimensions preserve different spatial scales; these methods are not interchangeable configuration names.

Evaluate both long-range retrieval and short-context quality. A larger maximum-position setting merely permits allocation; it does not demonstrate usable long-context reasoning. A cached key must use the same RoPE configuration as the query that reads it.
